sessionName: Week 9 - Keeping and growing PE relationships
summary: Luke Badiali led the retention and expansion session with Thomas Avery and Grace Lindqvist. Brookvale has worked for 26 PE houses in three years, but 8 of them account for most fees and two of those have gone quiet. We agreed to name key accounts, introduce a post-deal debrief and offer portfolio support work after completion.

discussion.keyPoints: Grace's list showed 26 PE houses and 8 giving 75 percent of fees. Two of the eight have not mandated Brookvale in 9 months, both after larger firms discounted.
Brookvale walks away once the CDD report is delivered. Luke noted the sponsor's 100-day plan often needs the same market work. Thomas thought portfolio work could smooth revenue.
No feedback is collected. Grace said deal partners prefer a short call to a survey.

recommendations.recommendation: Name all 8 top PE houses as key accounts, each owned by Thomas or a director, with a quarterly relationship review.
Offer a 100-day value creation market sprint to every sponsor that completes a deal, priced at 60k.
Hold a 20-minute debrief call with the deal partner within two weeks of every report.
Win back the two quiet key accounts with a free sector briefing session for their deal teams.
Ask satisfied deal partners for introductions to their portfolio company CEOs.

actions.action: Set up quarterly relationship reviews for the 8 key accounts
Book the free sector briefings with the two quiet key accounts

nextFocus: Build the financial model behind fees, pitch costs and the portfolio offer.
nextPreparation: Thomas to bring fee, utilisation and pitch time data for the last 12 months.

tests.question: How many key accounts did we name?
What is the price of the 100-day value creation market sprint?
Is the plan to win back the two quiet accounts agreed?
